scope: Kayenta Obsession second-edition base/core; standard 16-round multiplayer game, 2–4 players, base objective deck; expansions, optional variants and other modes excluded.

input_isolation.did_not_read: Summary, reader responses, grades, parent history, other reviewer reports and other QA files.
input_isolation.source_review: Read core setup and play/detail, all base-relevant FAQs, ordinary family/Fairchild/base unusual gentry entries, all improvement appendix entries with expansion scope separated, VP cards, and all base objective passages. Read corrigendum text, including the relevant seasonal market player-aid correction. Inspected PDF page 12 standard track image, page 111 objective card images, and page 28 image-only page (illustration).

factual_correctness.assessment: No demonstrated material factual contradiction found in Q01–Q56 against the scoped authoritative sources. This is not a saturation finding.

checked_high_risk_points.result: Base-only scope correctly excludes hiring as a passing benefit; the Butler’s Room remains an activity.
Seasonal full market refresh is the current default. Corrigendum explicitly identifies the old flowchart as incomplete.
PDF standard track confirms Village Fair at 3 and 9, Draw Objectives at 6, National Holiday at 14.
Base versus replacement objective decks were separated. The reputation objective shows the Max level counter; the key’s standard level-7 interpretation is consistent with that image.

minor_clarity_note.note: The key’s optional one-tile purchase is the ordinary default. It should be read with the Builders’ Holiday / Market Purchase exception already tested in Q32; adding “normally” would make this key entry self-contained. This is a wording clarification, not a new coverage addition.

coverage_findings.finding: Neither invitation handling nor attendance limits test the explicit absence of a hand/discard capacity limit.
The bank tests Reserve prices, movement and multiple purchases but never asks whether the entire Reserve is public and selectable.
Pass procedure is covered, but voluntary passing and the forced-pass outcome when no activity can be fulfilled are not explicitly tested.
The bank states the paid Refresh Market special action limit but does not test the FAQ’s express permission to perform separate passing-benefit and VP-card refreshes in the same turn.

proposed_additions.question: Is there a limit to the number of gentry cards in your hand or personal discard pile? If an invitation adds a guest to a large hand, must you discard or dismiss another card to make room?
proposed_additions.expected_answer: There is no limit to gentry cards in either your hand or your personal discard pile. Adding a guest does not require discarding or dismissing another card to make room.
proposed_additions.novelty_reason: New explicit capacity rule. Q36 limits attendees at one activity; Q37 explains drawing and revealing guests. Neither tests ownership/hand capacity or a forced replacement obligation.

proposed_additions.question: Tiles in the Builders’ Reserve are stacked with the tile you want underneath other tiles. May you inspect the Reserve now and later buy that buried tile, or must you buy only the top tile?
proposed_additions.expected_answer: The Reserve is public and may be inspected at any time. Its tiles may be stacked in any order or spread face up. You may buy any eligible affordable tile from it instead of a Market tile; there is no top-tile restriction. The usual price is £300 plus its modifier, with the £100 minimum and duplicate prohibition still applying.
proposed_additions.novelty_reason: New information/access rule and selection outcome. Q10 tests prices and duplicate/PR restrictions, Q12 opening and movement, and Q32 purchase counts. None asks whether a stacked Reserve restricts information or selection to the top tile.

proposed_additions.question: You cannot fulfill every requirement of the activity you initially wanted to host, but another activity in your tableau is legal. Must you host that other activity, or may you pass? What if you cannot fulfill any activity in your tableau?
proposed_additions.expected_answer: You cannot host an activity whose reputation, gentry or service requirements you cannot fulfill. You may choose a different legal activity or pass, even when another activity is available. If you cannot host any activity, you must pass.
proposed_additions.novelty_reason: New procedural choice and forced outcome branch from an otherwise untested source paragraph. Q03 describes how passing works, while Q02/Q31/Q36 describe hosting requirements; none explicitly tests when passing is voluntary versus mandatory.

proposed_additions.question: On an ordinary pass turn you take the free Market Refresh passing benefit and still want more market churn. May you also use the paid Refresh Market special action and Market Refresh VP cards in that same turn? Which of those refresh methods is limited to once per turn?
proposed_additions.expected_answer: Yes. The once-per-turn restriction applies to the paid Refresh Market special action only (cost 4 reputation, with sufficient reputation required). The separate passing benefit and each Market Refresh VP card can also refresh the Market that turn. Multiple VP cards may be used. Using those other methods does not authorize a second paid Refresh Market special action.
proposed_additions.novelty_reason: Explicit source-defined exception to the scope of a once-per-turn restriction. This tests whether the limit governs the named paid action or all outcomes that refresh the market, rather than merely combining arbitrary effects. Q06 names the limit but never exercises this different ruling; Q17 does not identify separate refresh permissions.

rejected_additions.candidate: Repeat opening monument / servant setup questions for two or three players, or change amounts and thresholds in existing examples.
rejected_additions.reason: Same rule-defined branch with altered numbers; Q23/Q25 already test the setup procedures.

rejected_additions.candidate: Ask every remaining base tile’s printed attendance counts, favour amounts, price modifiers and VP.
rejected_additions.reason: Ordinary data lookup or cosmetic tile substitution. Distinct base tile exceptions are already covered by Q07–Q09, Q18–Q20, Q43–Q46 and Q56.

rejected_additions.candidate: Add the remaining AND-style tile group objectives and servant thresholds as separate questions.
rejected_additions.reason: Q16/Q53 already establish possession-at-end and group satisfaction. Changing tile names or required servant counts creates no distinct timing, priority or exception branch.

rejected_additions.candidate: Ask whether a late-bought monument pays retroactively or a newly flipped suite pays reputation immediately.
rejected_additions.reason: Mechanical recombination of the existing step order, ongoing-effect timing and mandatory flipping rules (Q02/Q18/Q19/Q29); no separate exception in the source.

rejected_additions.candidate: Use a hybrid Estate activity with Barn to test a reputation award and subsequent category movement.
rejected_additions.reason: Mechanical recombination of Q18 face-up category/flip handling and Q43 Barn trigger, without a distinct exception.

rejected_additions.candidate: Spend money or reputation after final courtship and recompute wealth/reputation objectives.
rejected_additions.reason: Mechanical recombination of Q14/Q17 final action window and Q55 objective conditions.

rejected_additions.candidate: Add take-a-reminder-token-on-acquiring-an-ongoing-tile as a new scoring question.
rejected_additions.reason: The marker procedure is an uncovered physical aid detail (p.39, lines 1483–1488), but it has no distinct game-state outcome and is too cosmetic to justify a meaningful coverage addition.

rejected_additions.candidate: Add expansion guest-count modifiers, alternate West Terrace, Business Room, second-chance servants, houseguests, replacement objective majorities or solo upkeep.
rejected_additions.reason: Outside the specified base/core scope. The corrigendum’s Business Room and solo fixes do not add base-game questions.

conclusion: Original IDs are unique and matched, with no demonstrated material factual key correction required. Coverage is not saturated: four source-backed additions test core rules or expressly defined branches that the existing questions do not directly ask. Reassess these additions under the same strict novelty test before incorporating them; no claim of exhaustive saturation is made.
